## BaseFormatter.of() method

Formats a given value according to the formatter's configuration.

**Signature:**

```typescript
of<T extends bigint | null | undefined, D extends number | null | undefined>(value: T, decimals: D): Exclude<T, bigint> | Exclude<D, number> | string;
```

## Parameters

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

value


</td><td>

T


</td><td>

The value to format. It can be: - A `bigint` for precise numeric representation. - A `number` for floating-point or scientific notation input. - `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->, in which case the method will retain the nullability of the input unless a default value is set.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

decimals


</td><td>

D


</td><td>

If input value is a bigint. It can be `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->, in which case the method will retain the nullability of the input unless a default value is set.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Exclude&lt;T, bigint&gt; \| Exclude&lt;D, number&gt; \| string

The formatted value as a string, or: - The default value `value` or `decimals` is `null` or `undefined`<!-- -->. - `null`<!-- -->or `undefined` in case `value` or `decimals` is `null` or `undefined` and no default value is set

## Example 1

// Example with bigint input console.log(formatter.of(123456789n, 2)); // Output: "1234567.89"

## Example 2

// Example with number input console.log(formatter.of(123.45)); // Output: "123.45"

## Example 3

// Handling null or undefined console.log(formatter.of(null, 2)); // Output: null
